en: Where, like, I asked them both, when do you think AGI is coming?
zh: 那次，比如，我问他们俩，你们认为 AGI 什么时候会来？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Sergei's timeline was shorter than Temis's.
zh: 而 Sergei 的时间线比 Temis 的更短。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was this kind of interesting moment there, which was fun to see.
zh: 那里有这么一个挺有意思的时刻，看着很过瘾。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, speaking of guys who mistrust and maybe don't like each other, I understand there's some tension between Sergey and Demis.
zh: 我是说，说到那些互不信任、甚至可能互相讨厌的家伙，我听说 Sergey 和 Demis 之间有些紧张关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, it's incredibly messy.
zh: 是的，这真是极其混乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that animates all these feuds, like these people wouldn't be fighting if the stakes were small.
zh: 驱动所有这些争斗的东西是，如果赌注很小，这些人根本不会斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they believe this is the most important technology that humanity has ever conceived of and built.
zh: 但他们相信这是人类有史以来构想和建造的最重要技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that whoever gets it will be the most powerful person in the world, the most powerful entity in the world.
zh: 而且谁得到了它，谁就将是世界上最强大的人，世界上最强大的实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is what's fueling their drive.
zh: 这就是驱动他们前进的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, if they were just arguing about next quarter's revenue, it wouldn't matter so much.
zh: 你知道，如果他们只是在争论下个季度的营收，就没那么重要了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this to them is like existentially important.
zh: 但对他们来说，这关乎存亡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree?
zh: 你同意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That AI is the most important thing ever created?
zh: 同意 AI 是有史以来最被创造出来的最重要的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably.
zh: 大概吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fire is up there too.
zh: 火也算一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like this part of it, I do think I changed my mind on in the core.
zh: 但就这部分而言，我确实在最核心的看法上改变了主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was pretty skeptical when I went in that like AI was going to be categorically different than other.
zh: 我一开始很怀疑，觉得 AI 会和其他东西有本质上的不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was sort of an AI as normal technology guy.
zh: 我原本算是个「AI 不过是普通技术」派。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you start talking to people building this, you start understanding like just the nature of what they're trying to do.
zh: 但后来你开始和建造这个东西的人交谈，你开始理解他们想要做的事情的本质。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like if it works,
zh: 然后比如，如果它成功了，

speaker: Unknown
en: If they actually do build something that is smarter than humans, and I don't see any real technical reason that they can't, I mean, that would be incredibly transformative.
zh: 如果他们真的造出了比人类更聪明的东西——而我看不出有什么真正的技术原因说他们做不到——我是说，那将是极具变革性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've never been the second smartest species on the planet before.
zh: 我们以前从来没有做过地球上第二聪明的物种。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't know how that would go and you can't really apply like people say, oh, it's just like the internet or it's just like the steam engine.
zh: 我们不知道那会怎样，而且你没法真的套用——人们会说，哦，它就像互联网，或者它就像蒸汽机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Steam engines didn't go rogue and like hack competitors and develop bio weapons and do things that the engineers building the steam engines didn't expect or plan for.
zh: 蒸汽机可没有变得失控、去黑竞争对手、开发生物武器、做那些建造蒸汽机的工程师们没有预料到或没有计划到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's just a different type of technology.
zh: 所以我觉得它就是一种不同类型的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kevin, do you ever think to yourself, like maybe, and I've seen your, you've been on X and, you know, I wouldn't say shouting at people, but telling people basically like, underestimate this technology at your own risk.
zh: Kevin，你有没有想过，比如——我看过你在 X 上——你知道的，我不会说是冲人喊，但基本上是在告诉人们：低估这项技术风险自负。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's been so weird, because like, on one level, I'm a journalist.
zh: 是啊，这感觉很奇怪，因为，在一个层面上，我是个记者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm just trying to like, get the story down.
zh: 比如，我只是想把故事记录下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at the same time, I get incredibly frustrated when people are like, oh, it's all hype.
zh: 而与此同时，当有人说「哦，全是炒作」「只是营销」时，我会感到极度沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just marketing.
zh: 有这么一种——

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this kind of like,
zh: 有这么一种自以为精明的东海岸共识，觉得这些人多多少少肯定在胡扯，他们造的东西不可能真的强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Savvy East Coast consensus that like these people have to be full of shit on some level and that the thing that they're building can't actually be powerful.
zh: 而我就想，你用过它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, have you used it?
zh: 比如，你花时间用过这些工具吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you spend time with these tools?
zh: 你明白吗，三年前连基本数学都做不了的东西，现在正在解决千禧年大奖难题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you understand that like something that couldn't do basic math like three years ago is now solving millennium prize problems?
zh: 比如，你理解这个指数曲线吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, do you understand the exponential?
zh: 对我来说，这有点像 COVID 初期，当时你会看到这些报道，比如风投公司的人不握手了，或者说，有人会说，哦，西雅图有 40 个病例。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels a little bit to me like the beginning days of COVID where it was like you would see these reports of like people, you know, not shaking hands at venture capital firms or they're, you know, somebody would say, oh, there are 40 cases in Seattle.
zh: 然后人们会说，这有什么大不了的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And people would be like, what's the big deal?
zh: 才 40 个病例，在西雅图而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 40 cases in Seattle.
zh: （原文至此）

speaker: Unknown
en: But the people who are freaking out were like the epidemiologists who saw the rate of replication and understood like
zh: 但那些真正慌了的人，就像那些看到复制速度并理解的流行病学家，

speaker: Unknown
en: This will continue and when it does like a month from now there will be millions of cases and two months from now there'll be millions more cases.
zh: 这会继续下去，当它发生时，比如一个月后就会有数百万病例，两个月后还会有数百万更多的病例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I feel like the people who are looking at this technology and saying like what's the big deal are just not understanding the rate of progress.
zh: 所以我觉得那些看着这项技术说这有什么大不了的人，只是没有理解进步的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you ever like ask yourself, I mean, it's sometimes very easy to be, and I agree with you, there's been real progress, but it's also sometimes easy to kind of get caught up in the story that the technologists tell.
zh: 你有没有问过自己，我是说，有时候很容易——我同意你的看法，确实有真正的进步——但有时候也很容易陷入技术专家讲述的那种故事里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember you like,
zh: 我记得你，

speaker: Unknown
en: When crypto was in vogue, you were very serious about the potential of crypto, you named your podcast Hard Fork, which was a crypto term, and then obviously that didn't pan out as the crypto boosters believed.
zh: 当加密货币流行的时候，你对加密货币的潜力是非常认真的，你把你的播客命名为 Hard Fork,那是一个加密货币术语，然后显然事情并没有像加密货币的拥护者所相信的那样发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do you think there could be a similar, do you ever wonder if you're basically taking the AI folks' word for it similarly as the crypto folks?
zh: 所以你认为会不会有类似的情况，你有没有想过你基本上是在像相信加密货币那些人一样，轻信了 AI 那些人的话？

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to think that.
zh: 我曾经是这么想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used to worry about that because I was like, am I being duped here?
zh: 我曾经担心这个，因为我会在想，我是不是在这里被骗了？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was never a crypto booster, but I thought it was interesting.
zh: 我从来不是加密货币的拥护者，但我觉得它很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought people should take it seriously.
zh: 我觉得人们应该认真对待它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, I still think people should take it seriously because crypto people run the country now and are doing all kinds of scams and frauds that only the insiders kind of understand.
zh: 顺便说一句，我仍然认为人们应该认真对待它，因为加密货币的人现在在管理这个国家，正在做各种只有内部人才看得懂的骗局和欺诈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I still think broader awareness of that would be good.
zh: 所以我仍然认为让更广泛的人意识到这一点是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, but you believed in use cases.
zh: 对，但你相信它的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did some experiments, like I sold an NFT as a stunt, but that was not like me saying NFTs are gonna be the future of ownership.
zh: 我做过一些实验，比如我作为一个噱头卖过一个 NFT,但那并不代表我说 NFT 会是所有权的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like me trying to understand by doing the thing.
zh: 那更像是我试图通过亲自做这件事来理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think with AI, like I have stopped.
zh: 但我觉得对于 AI,我已经不再——

speaker: Unknown
en: Doubting the transformative potential of the products because I use them.
zh: 怀疑这些产品的变革潜力了，因为我亲自使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I think I'm unlike many journalists who cover AI in that I like AI and I use it all the time, not to write, but to like do all, you know, I'm starting a company now.
zh: 就是说，我想我和很多报道 AI 的记者不一样，我喜欢 AI,我一直都在用它，不是用来写作，而是用来做各种事情，你知道，我现在正在创办一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I use it to do lots of different things as maybe you do too.
zh: 就像，我用它来做很多不同的事情，也许你也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, as a business owner, I will say, like, I've pressure tested the stuff from ChatGPT 2022 till now.
zh: 我是说，作为一个企业主，我可以说，从 2022 年的 ChatGPT 到现在，我对这些东西做过压力测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just does more and more and more for me.
zh: 它为我做的事情越来越多越来越多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, which is not the experience that anyone had with crypto, where it's like, oh, this is a vital part of my daily life.
zh: 对，这是任何人在加密货币上都没有过的体验，比如说，哦，这是我日常生活中不可或缺的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it was a way to speculate.
zh: 它是一种投机的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can just use the tools and observe for yourself how impressive they are.
zh: 但你可以直接使用这些工具，亲自观察它们有多令人印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you'd stop doubting whether it's real.
zh: 然后你就会停止怀疑它是不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I buy the skepticism about the financial models of these companies, the economic impacts.
zh: 对于这些公司的财务模型、经济影响，我接受这种怀疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of these companies are wrong or at least could be wrong about the impact of AI on jobs.
zh: 我觉得很多这些公司在 AI 对就业的影响上是错的，或者至少可能是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But to say that it's not interesting, transformative technology just means that you haven't spent time with the models because there's no way to conclude that.
zh: 但要说它不是一项有趣的、变革性的技术，那只说明你没有花时间使用过这些模型，因为不可能得出那样的结论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get back to some of these stories.
zh: 我们回到其中一些故事吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Sam-Demis rivalry.
zh: Sam 和 Demis 的竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of Demis as the most competitive person on Earth, I think Sam is also fairly competitive.
zh: 说到 Demis 是地球上最好胜的人，我觉得 Sam 也相当好胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a great anecdote in the book about Demis sort of...
zh: 书里有一个很精彩的轶事，讲 Demis 有点——

speaker: Unknown
en: Grasping at why Sam wants to build AGI.
zh: 想要搞明白 Sam 为什么想构建 AGI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think the answer is probably because Sam is an entrepreneur and this is sort of as many people in the Valley pursue good ideas or ideas with potential and they sort of get off on that discovery.
zh: 我是说，我觉得答案大概是因为 Sam 是一个创业者，就像硅谷很多人一样追求好点子或者有潜力的想法，他们从那种发现中获得快感。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sam seems to be in that case, the ability to find something new, build it.
zh: 在这个例子里，Sam 似乎就是那种，能够发现新东西，然后把它构建出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But demos can't understand it.
zh: 但 Demis 无法理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: He thinks there's a hidden motive with Sam.
zh: 他认为 Sam 背后有隐藏的动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be fair, this is something that others have thought.
zh: 说句公道话，这也是其他人想过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is also what Dario thought about Sam when they worked together, that he was sort of, I don't know, talking about safety as kind of a fig leaf for his real ambition, which was about scaling or winning or building a huge company or something like that.
zh: 这也是 Dario 在和 Sam 共事时对他的看法，就是他，我不知道，把安全当作遮羞布来谈，掩盖他真正的野心，那是关于扩张、或者赢、或者建一家巨大的公司之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't pretend to like see inside Sam's mind.
zh: 所以我不会假装能看透 Sam 的内心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what his pure motive is, but
zh: 我不知道他纯粹的动机是什么，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in Demis' case, he feels like his own pursuit of AGI is motivated by like scientific curiosity and sort of this inevitability argument, like this technology will be built and someone who cares about safety and the collective good of this technology should build it.
zh: 我觉得在 Demis 的情况下，他觉得自己追求 AGI 的动机是出于科学好奇心，加上一种必然性论证，比如这项技术终将被构建出来，而一个关心安全和这项技术集体利益的人应该去构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think everyone kind of looks at each other in this world, and they're like, well, my motives are pure, but like, that guy must be going after something else.
zh: 但我觉得在这个圈子里，每个人都会互相打量，然后说，好吧，我的动机是纯粹的，但那家伙肯定是在追求别的什么东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for Demis, it's probably, yeah, some version of what you said, like he's, you know, he's in it for the power, or he's... Demis thinks Sam is in it for the power.
zh: 我觉得对 Demis 来说，大概就是你说的那种版本的看法，比如，你知道，他是为了权力，或者他是……Demis 认为 Sam 是为了权力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Demis thinks Sam is in it for the power, yes.
zh: 我觉得 Demis 认为 Sam 是为了权力，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But all these guys think that the other people are in it for the power.
zh: 但所有这些人也都认为别人是为了权力。

speaker: Unknown
en: None of them trust that anyone else's motives are pure except for their own.
zh: 除了他们自己，他们不信任任何其他人的动机是纯粹的。

en: You did a lot of reporting on Sam.
zh: 你对 Sam 做了大量报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You spoke to Ilya about him.
zh: 你和 Ilya 谈过他。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ilya said that he displayed a consistent pattern of lying.
zh: Ilya 说他表现出一种持续撒谎的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's something that I think you indicate a lot of people within OpenAI or who've interacted with him believe.
zh: 我认为这表明 OpenAI 内部或与他打过交道的很多人都这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet, and I think Mir Marati was on that boat as well.
zh: 而且，我觉得 Mir Marati 也在那条船上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet...
zh: 然而……

speaker: Unknown
en: They all sort of come back to him.
zh: 他们最终都又回到了他身边。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Ilya, after the coup, said, basically, I don't want Sam to be the leader.
zh: 我是说，Ilya 在政变之后说过，基本上，我不想要 Sam 当领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Miura said, opening eyes, nothing without its people.
zh: Miura 说过，OpenAI 离了它的人就什么都不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very interesting character.
zh: 非常有趣的人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your thought about Sam?
zh: 你对 Sam 的看法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he's a very interesting character.
zh: 我觉得他是一个非常有趣的人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that Sam's superpower is also his weakness.
zh: 我认为 Sam 的超能力同时也是他的弱点。

speaker: Unknown
en: His superpower is that he is the world's greatest fundraiser and salesman, entrepreneur.
zh: 他的超能力是，他是世界上最伟大的募资者、销售员和创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Several people described him as a person who can
zh: 好几个人把他描述成这样一个人，能够

speaker: Unknown
en: meet you and figure out exactly what you want and give it to you, or at least appear to give it to you.
zh: 见到你并准确弄清楚你想要什么，然后把它给你，或者至少看起来给了你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's very good at kind of high EQ reading the room and understanding what people want him to do in any given moment.
zh: 而且他非常擅长高情商地察言观色，在任何时刻理解人们想让他做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is a huge asset for him when he's trying to raise money from someone like Massa Son or some of the other investors in OpenAI.
zh: 当他试图从孙正义或 OpenAI 的其他一些投资者那里募资时，这是他巨大的资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's allowed them to scale incredibly quickly and get back in the good graces of the Trump administration by just saying a lot of things that the Trump administration wanted to hear.
zh: 这让他们能够以难以置信的速度扩张，并且仅仅通过说很多 Trump 政府想听的话，就重新赢得了 Trump 政府的好感。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it also leads to this reputation as like a slippery people pleaser who will just like tell one thing to one person and a completely different thing to someone else.
zh: 但这也导致了这样一种名声，就像一个滑头的讨好者，会对一个人说一件事，又对另一个完全不同的人说完全不同的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is the consistent pattern that people have identified in SAM for going back to literally the founding days of OpenAI.
zh: 所以这就是人们在 Sam 身上识别出的那种持续模式，可以一直追溯到 OpenAI 真正创立之初。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a big part of the reason that Dario and his six co-founders of Anthropic left.
zh: 而这也是 Dario 和他在 Anthropic 的六位联合创始人离开的一个重要原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was no like inciting incident, no single thing, but it was just like a running list of like times where Sam had told them something that he had told something else to someone else or he made a promise he didn't follow through on.
zh: 没有什么导火索事件，没有任何单一的事情，而只是一份不断累积的清单，上面记着 Sam 对他们说了一套、又对别人说了另一套的时刻，或者他做了承诺却没有兑现的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think depending on your view of Sam, it's like either his superpower or his liability or something in between.
zh: 所以我认为，取决于你对 Sam 的看法，这要么是他的超能力，要么是他的软肋，或者介于两者之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, what's interesting is that that's the view of people who've dealt with him, but it's also like he has like the general public, a large chunk of them sort of refer to him as Scam Altman.
zh: 是的，有意思的是，这是那些和他打过交道的人的看法，但同时，公众中很大一部分人也把他称作 Scam Altman(骗子奥特曼)。

en: That's just an Elon thing, right?
zh: 那只是 Elon 搞出来的，对吧？

en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because him and Elon obviously have bad blood.
zh: 因为他跟 Elon 显然有过节。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I will say, Scam Altman is a better nickname than what I think Elon started calling him when he started suing him, which was like, Swindly Sam or something like that.
zh: 是的，我要说，Scam Altman 这个绰号比我想象中 Elon 开始起诉他时给他起的那个要好，那个好像是 Swindly Sam 还是之类的。

en: I would love for our society to just get, just to not do this to each other anymore.
